name: Médoc

limits: For white wine, Alvarinho, Floréal, Liliorila, Sauvignac and Souvignier Gris together: at most 5%
For red wine, Arinarnoa, Castets, Marselan and Touriga Nacional together: at most 5%

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

terms: France's protected place names. A wine sold under one must follow that appellation's rules. The EU's term for the same tier is PDO, or AOP in French.
Indication Géographique Protégée, the tier below AOC. It replaced vin de pays in 2009.
France's simplest category, in use since 2010. It replaced vin de table.
There is no legal or agreed definition of old, so the words promise nothing on their own.
One of the two regional appellations allowed anywhere in Bordeaux, beside plain Bordeaux. Together they cover about half the Bordeaux vineyard.

In 1855 brokers ranked Bordeaux estates by reputation and price. Reds were ranked from first to fifth growths, nearly all in the Médoc, and the sweet whites of Sauternes and Barsac from superior first growth to second growth.
A ranking for Médoc châteaux left out of the 1855 classification. Any Médoc property may apply.
keyfacts: Médoc AOC may be used across 50 communes of the Médoc peninsula, on the Left Bank north of Bordeaux, but it is claimed mainly in the north, the area once called Bas-Médoc.
Soils are gravel laid down by the Garonne and Dordogne and Tertiary clay-limestone, with Cabernet Sauvignon favoring the gravel and Cabernet Franc the limestone.
Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot are the main grapes, with Petit Verdot, Malbec, Cabernet Franc and Carmenère also allowed.
Large châteaux sit beside small family estates backed by several cooperatives, and no estate under the Médoc appellation was included in the 1855 classification.

notes: Petit Verdot is used in small amounts here to give structure to the Bordeaux blend.

blurb.text: A Left Bank Bordeaux appellation whose zone covers the whole Médoc peninsula, though in practice the name is used mainly in the north, sometimes called Bas-Médoc. It is almost all red, from Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Cabernet Franc and others, with a small but growing amount of white.
